r3-evidence.title: Required evidence
r3-evidence.imperative: Is the required evidence present and does it actually demonstrate the behavior? Priority order per handoff: (1) one mutation the implementer did not choose, run against -k 'map_tree_freshness'; (2) tc20 -- confirm or refute whether the ids.jsonl half of the test is a check that cannot fail; (3) does the 2-file landing zone as shipped actually resolve. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r3-evidence.finding:
PASS. All three priority items addressed with direct, reverted-and-verified probes.

=== Priority 1: an untried mutation against -k 'map_tree_freshness' ===

Ran THREE mutations the implementer did not choose (their two were: staling the
committed index directly, and a shape edit -- new top-level function -- to
scripts/agent_work_root.py left un-rebuilt):

(a) Docstring reword, scripts/code_map/discovery.py:is_mappable -- reworded the
one-line docstring, no signature/shape/count change. Result: BOTH tests stayed
GREEN. This is CORRECT, not blind: landing-zone-measurement.md's Arm A already
predicted a body-only edit must not move the root index (root INDEX.md carries
only per-module entity counts and each module's own docstring first line, not
per-function summaries), and the implementer's own shape-edit mutation (already
in evidence) proves the same selector CAN go RED when the corpus genuinely
changes shape. So this is a true negative, not an untested blind spot.

(b) Symbol rename, scripts/agent_work_root.py: `_normalize` -> `_normalize_renamed_probe`
(def line only). Result: BOTH tests stayed GREEN. Confirms root INDEX.md's
committed scope is aggregate counts only, not per-symbol names -- a rename does
not change any number the root index carries, so this is in-scope behavior
(the root page never claimed per-symbol accuracy; a crew regenerates the body
locally before trusting per-symbol content). Worth naming as a scope boundary,
not a defect -- see Out-of-scope observations.

(c) Added a genuine authored anchor comment (`# [gs-review-probe-anchor]`) above
scripts/code_map/discovery.py:is_mappable -- the actual `ANCHOR` regex this tool
extracts ids from (extract.py's `anchors_in`), not a synthetic file edit. Result:
test_map_tree_freshness_ids_jsonl_matches_a_fresh_build went RED
(committed '' != fresh '{"id": "gs-review-probe-anchor", "s":
"scripts.code_map.discovery:is_mappable"}\n'); the root-index sibling stayed
GREEN (an id addition doesn't move aggregate counts). This is priority 2's
direct answer -- see below.

All three mutations reverted via `git checkout --`, each confirmed byte-clean
via `git diff --quiet -- <path>` (not `git status --porcelain`, per the
handoff's own CRLF warning). I also independently reproduced the implementer's
OWN claimed staled-index mutation (appended a marker line to committed
map/INDEX.md; selector went RED with the exact diff-length AssertionError shape
claimed in gs-implement-RESULT.md; reverted, byte-clean) rather than accepting
their report on its own word, per this repo's verify-claimed-side-effects
doctrine.

=== Priority 2: tc20 -- confirm or refute ===

REFUTED as stated, confirmed with a real counter-example: the ids.jsonl half is
NOT a check that cannot fail. Mutation (c) above shows it goes RED on the one
axis it actually exists to guard -- an authored anchor id landing in the corpus
without the committed ids.jsonl being rebuilt. I also directly corrupted the
committed file (wrote a fake JSON line into map/ids.jsonl, no source change) and
confirmed RED that way too (both reverted, byte-clean).

The narrower, true observation behind tc20 stands and is worth keeping precise:
it has never yet been EXERCISED by real history, because zero anchors have ever
been authored in this repo (a fact g6 already established), and neither of the
implementer's own two chosen mutations happened to touch the anchor axis --
that is a coverage gap in which mutations were DEMONSTRATED, not a defect in
the test's design. The test correctly discriminates when given the input class
it exists for; this repo has simply never produced that input class yet.

=== Priority 3: does the 2-file landing zone as shipped resolve? ===

Yes. `git ls-files map/` returns exactly `map/INDEX.md` + `map/ids.jsonl`.
`git check-ignore -v` exits 1 (NOT ignored) on both; exits 0 (ignored, matched
by `map/*`) on a sampled body page (`map/scripts.code_map/INDEX.md`) -- the
.gitignore rule (priority 4) does exactly what it claims: never silently tracks
body pages, never silently ignores the two shipped files. map/INDEX.md itself
is well-formed (147 lines, package/module sections, working relative links into
`<module>/INDEX.md`). Those per-module links do not resolve until a build runs
-- confirmed as the accepted, pre-named limitation, not a new finding.

r6-fowler.imperative: Run the refactoring / code-smell pass (SKILL.md 'Refactoring pass'). Render a verdict on each Fowler baseline smell (long method, large class, duplicated code, feature envy, data clumps, primitive obsession, long parameter list, shotgun surgery, divergent change, message chains, speculative generality, comments-as-deodorant): flagged / overridden / absent. Smells are judgment calls, ALWAYS subordinate to the repo's documented standards -- an override needs a logged standard + reason. Record the pass to templates/FOWLER_PASS.template.json, run scripts/verify_fowler_pass.py <record> (it refuses a skipped smell or an unlogged override), then record pass/fail with a finding. This item's postcondition command ships with a <fowler-pass-record-path> placeholder; record() runs that command and refuses `pass` while it fails. NORMAL PATH -- resolve the placeholder to the real record path when you INSTANTIATE this survey from the template, before you claim: it is an instantiation-time substitution exactly like <work-id> on line 2. That is the documented route and the one you should be on. REPAIR PATH -- only if the record later moves or the path you substituted was wrong, correct it through the engine with `amend --delta <file>` whose single op is `retext-check` on this item's c1, never by hand-editing this survey. There, --authority is the dispatching Commander named in your reviewer handoff (never a string you invent), and --reason is why the path changed. Do NOT silently skip this item.
